faqs.q: How much does a Afghan Hound cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Afghan Hound puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Afghan Hound, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Afghan Hounds due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Afghan Hound cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Afghan Hound are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds need brushing 3–4 times per week to prevent matting.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Afghan Hounds shed a lot?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Afghan Hound need?
faqs.a: A wide-tooth comb, pin brush, and detangling spray are the core tools for a Afghan Hound's long coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for complete at-home maintenance.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Afghan Hounds that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Afghan Hounds easy to train?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds are moderately easy to train. They respond well to positive reinforcement and benefit from early puppy classes. Consistency from all household members is key.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Afghan Hounds. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: Most Afghan Hounds reliably perform basic cues within 4–6 weeks of daily 10–15 minute sessions. Reliable recall off-lead typically takes 3–4 months of progressive distance and distraction training.

faqs.q: What health problems do Afghan Hounds commonly have?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds are most commonly associated with ear infections. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Afghan Hounds live?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds have an average lifespan of 12–15 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Afghan Hounds prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Afghan Hounds than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Afghan Hound at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Afghan Hound puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Afghan Hound puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Afghan Hound-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Afghan Hounds good with kids?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds can do well with children when properly socialised from puppyhood. Every dog is an individual — early exposure to children's behaviour (noise, sudden movements) is the most effective preparation.

faqs.q: Do Afghan Hounds get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Afghan Hounds bark a lot?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Afghan Hounds good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Afghan Hound need per day?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Afghan Hounds good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Afghan Hounds make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Afghan Hound doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Afghan Hounds often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Afghan Hound be off-lead?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: A Afghan Hound needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: Adult Afghan Hounds should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Afghan Hounds benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Afghan Hound from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Afghan Hounds can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Afghan Hound a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Afghan Hounds good family dogs?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds can be excellent family dogs for active households. They thrive with children who can match their energy level. A calm household with limited exercise may not suit this breed's temperament.

faqs.q: Do Afghan Hounds do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Afghan Hounds form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Afghan Hound?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Afghan Hound — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
